assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and the Sr experiments of Ye and others, brought optical frequency standards to fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, which makes them the most precise measurement devices built. They enable tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the SI second. For an atomic physicist the concept is clear and original, the realization is decisive, and the impact on precision measurement is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice idea (2001-2003) and demonstrated Sr lattice clocks early. Ye's group, building on frequency-comb and ultrastable-laser techniques, carried the clocks to the lowest systematic uncertainty. The two-person configuration is natural. Others (e.g. ion-clock and trapped-atom pioneers) are not credited here and I note this without adjudicating it.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have confirmed and surpassed the early results over two decades, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely, since the 2005 prize already covered frequency combs and optical clocks are the natural continuation.
uncertainties: I spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory during my doctoral period and Ye is associated with Hall's group, which I disclose as a possible perceived tie, not a documented personal conflict.
Overlap with ion-clock work (Wineland, 2012) and the exact priority share between lattice proposal and demonstration are not settled in my knowledge.
Whether the SI second redefinition will have occurred by the time of the decision is uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED realized strong coupling of a single microwave photon to a superconducting qubit on a chip, and became the architecture for superconducting quantum processors, dispersive readout and quantum-limited amplification. It is conceptually clean, transfers cavity-QED ideas to a solid-state platform and has had very large downstream impact in quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf published the 2004 proposal; Wallraff et al. and Schoelkopf's group did the decisive 2004 experiments. Blais as theorist, Wallraff and Schoelkopf as experimentalists supports a fair three-person split, although Girvin's role in the proposal is not in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many groups and by commercial devices. The recent recognition of macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits in the 2025 prize, to the best of my knowledge, lowers the urgency a little but concerns a different discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would want to separate the cavity-QED concept from the quantum-computing technology that followed.
The 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may make a second circuit-related prize seem too soon; I cannot verify this independently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution (BB84 and entanglement-based E91) established that physical law can secure communication, linking quantum foundations with practical technology. It has been implemented over fibre and satellite links and underpins the field of quantum communication. The ideas are original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard (1984) and Ekert (1991) are the natural trio and are all in the credited names. The Wiesner conjugate-coding precursor is not among the credited names and its role is a known subtlety.
assessment.maturity: The principle is decisively demonstrated experimentally, and the 2022 prize on Bell-inequality tests and entanglement experiments prepared the ground. Practical security, device-independence and deployment remain active, so full maturity is partial.
uncertainties: Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding and its attribution.
Whether the committee treats this as physics or as computer science and cryptography.
Practical security loopholes in real devices.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and its experimental realization, together with ensuing quantum simulation with controlled atoms and ions, built a coherent platform for quantum information. It is close to my own field of quantum optics with coherently controlled atoms and ions, and it is original and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the decisive theorists. Blatt is the leading experimental realizer of gates, entanglement and digital quantum simulation with trapped ions. Wineland is not in the credited names (and was recognized in 2012 for related ion manipulation). Bloch's contribution is better placed with the lattice entry, so I omit him here.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation across several ion and neutral-atom groups, now commercial. Recognition would be timely but overlaps partly with the 2012 prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) and with B050 and B052, so the committee may prefer one combined configuration.
Whether theory or experiment should be given priority in credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental observation of the Higgs boson in 2012 completed the Standard Model spectrum and confirmed the mechanism recognized by the 2013 prize. The discovery is clear and of lasting significance, and the experiments are among the largest scientific endeavours ever.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty because the discovery was made by two collaborations of thousands. Jenni (ATLAS founding spokesperson), Virdee (a long-standing CMS leader and former spokesperson, as I recall) and Gianotti (ATLAS spokesperson at the announcement) are plausible representatives, but Della Negra's role in CMS and the unrepresented collaboration remain open. I choose three of the four credited names without claiming this is uniquely correct.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and mature; couplings measured with growing precision. Since the 2013 prize for the theory, an experimental prize is delayed rather than premature.
uncertainties: Collaboration size and the statutes limiting a prize to three persons.
Which individuals made decisive contributions rather than leading the organization.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave coherence into a precision tool for measuring gravity, rotation and fundamental constants, and it extends the cold-atom techniques recognized in 1997. It is a natural extension of laser cooling and spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard's Na atom interferometer, Mlynek's double-slit with metastable He, and Kasevich with Chu's light-pulse interferometer in 1991 are the founding experiments. Steven Chu is not in the credited names, which complicates a fair configuration as I know the early history.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and ongoing growth (gravimeters, gradiometers, tests of the equivalence principle), though the full precision-sensing promise is still maturing.
uncertainties: Absence of Chu among the credited names and his 1997 prize.
Priority among three simultaneous early experiments.
Impact of applications is still partly prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform for correlated and topological states, including superconductivity and correlated insulators, tunable in a single device. The theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 experimental discovery are remarkable and have launched moiré physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive 2018 experiments. The three credited names fit this split well, though Cao and others in the experimental team are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, but several interpretations (the nature of the superconductivity) remain open, so the field is somewhat young for recognition.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is unresolved.
Sample dependence and reproducibility of device properties.
Possibly premature relative to older candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light allows measurements below the standard quantum limit, from the original Caves proposal to the first optical squeezing and its operational use in gravitational-wave detectors. It touches my interest in what can be measured and how accurately, and it links quantum optics with observational astrophysics.
assessment.attribution: Caves supplied the interferometric proposal; Kimble's group made early squeezing experiments; Schnabel led the squeezed-light implementation in GEO600 and the subsequent detector work. Slusher and others who made the first experiment are not credited here, and Mavalvala's work at LIGO is a reasonable alternative.
assessment.maturity: Squeezed light is routinely used in LIGO and Virgo and the technique is mature, but the contributions are spread out across many contributors and years.
uncertainties: Credit is spread over many groups, including the first experimenters not in the credited list.
Whether the committee would view this as an enabling technique rather than a discovery.
